# Using SETTLE and KANERVA through settle-mcp

## Run a program

`run_program` takes a `path` to a `.settle` file or the program text as `source`, and returns what it printed, its errors and its exit code. Text runs in a fresh temporary folder.

A failing program exits with status 2 and prints `settle: line N: <message>`. Hand that line to `explain_error`, with the program as `source` to see the line it names.

## Start from a tested example

`list_examples` lists the tested programs from the SETTLE docs; `get_example` shows one with the exact output the interpreter is tested to print. Each is also a resource, `settle://examples/<name>`.

## Store and recall with a sparse distributed memory

`sdm_store_recall` writes named patterns, or short texts, into a sparse distributed memory and reads one back from a noisy read-address. It writes a short SETTLE program with the `sdm` statements, which call the KANERVA crate, and shows that program in its reply.

`noise` is the share of the read-address bits flipped before the read. A small noise comes back; near 0.4 the read stops finding the pattern, because the basins are narrow. `size` (bits, default 256) and `locations` (hard locations, default 2000) shape the memory.

The statement words it writes are read from the installed interpreter's `settle --help`, so the program always matches the SETTLE you built.

## Run KANERVA on its own

`kanerva_quickstart` runs the crate's own example, `cargo run --release --example quickstart`, in the kanerva folder setup made. Pass `dry_run` true to see the command without running it.

## Look a word up

`help` with a `topic` searches a glossary built from the site and its docs: statements, families, tokens, the words the docs define in bold, KANERVA modules, the site vocabulary, and KANERVA's terms file when it exists. The same list is the resource `settle-mcp://glossary`.
